sections.title: Colored Jones polynomial of figure eight knot and non-perturbative topological recursion
sections.abstract: The authors prove that the all-orders asymptotic expansion of the figure-eight knot's colored Jones polynomial is related to non-perturbative topological recursion on its elliptic spectral curve.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1.1 identifies the logarithmic differentials of the colored-Jones asymptotic wave function, its recurrence wave function, and a matched non-perturbative recursion wave function to all stable orders.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The result concerns the figure-eight knot and the specified elliptic spectral curve; the asymptotic expansion is established for q = exp(x/N) in a stated local domain and on a chosen branch.
sections.unique_caveat: The comparison is local and asymptotic, with analytic domains requiring care; the paper does not establish the result for general knots.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 1.00, entirely from four cross-lists (weight 0.25 each), tied for the highest available score. The explicit knot-invariant/topological-recursion bridge breaks the tie; no social-attention or citation component was recorded.

sections.title: Noise-induced Extinction in Hierarchical Food Webs
sections.abstract: For hierarchical food webs with omnivory, the authors develop a large-deviation account of demographic-noise-driven extinction networks and derive recursive formulas for mean extinction times.
sections.claimed_result: Under the stated model, the authors classify feasible communities and their stability, obtain closed-form fluctuational fixed points, and derive an exact recursion for mean extinction times over a network with 3^(N-1) transitions; for three species they compute instanton actions numerically and compare routes with stochastic simulations.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The model has a basal reproducing species, consumers may prey on all species below them, conversion efficiency is one, and self-limitation acts only on the basal species; the general-N analysis restricts parameters to fixed-point attractors and assumes feasibility of the candidate fixed points.
sections.unique_caveat: For general N the authors do not rule out non-stationary attractors on the invariant set they identify, and the worked three-species instanton actions are numerical rather than closed-form.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 1.00 from four cross-lists, tied for the highest available score; dynamical systems and probability are among the mathematical cross-lists. The general-N result and worked three-species analysis place it second among the tied top-score entries. No social-attention or citation component was recorded.

sections.title: Equivariant K-homology of affine Grassmannians of orthogonal groups
sections.abstract: The authors construct symmetric-function models for torus-equivariant K-homology of affine Grassmannians in types B and D, representing Schubert structure-sheaf and boundary ideal-sheaf classes.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 5.2 identifies the torus-equivariant K-homology algebra in types B and D with an algebra of constructed symmetric functions, matching Schubert structure sheaves and boundary ideal sheaves to explicit elements.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The construction is for torus-equivariant K-homology of affine Grassmannians of orthogonal types B and D, retaining the equivariant parameters.
sections.unique_caveat: In type D, specializing the equivariant parameters to zero identifies distinct Schubert classes; the authors conjecture a description of the resulting kernel rather than proving it.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 0.75 from three cross-lists (weight 0.25 each), the strongest score tier below the two four-cross-list papers. The explicit type-B/D realization distinguishes it within the tier; no social-attention or citation component was recorded.

sections.title: Fast Algorithms for Permanents of Permutationally-Dominant Matrices
sections.abstract: The authors give a fully polynomial randomized approximation scheme for permanents of permutationally-dominant matrices, using a polymer representation and importance sampling.
sections.claimed_result: The abstract claims an FPRAS with runtime quadratic in both matrix dimension and inverse approximation error, using a polymer-model representation and importance sampling of the logarithm of its partition function.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The guarantee applies to the paper's class of permutationally-dominant matrices.
sections.unique_caveat: The stated runtime is restricted to that matrix class; the abstract does not claim a fast approximation scheme for arbitrary permanents.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 0.75 from three cross-lists, including discrete mathematics; its explicit approximation guarantee makes it a strong algorithmic result in this tier. No social-attention or citation component was recorded.

sections.title: Higher-Dimensional Automata in Geometric Logic
sections.abstract: The authors encode partial higher-dimensional automata and their infinite runs in geometric logic, showing that the resulting label topos can distinguish machines with the same Büchi language and frame.
sections.claimed_result: For finite rigid machines over alphabets with decidable equality, the authors characterize unambiguity by inclusion of locale label maps and show that equivalence over the label topos is decidable when either machine is unambiguous.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The framework uses partial higher-dimensional automata, geometric theories over an intuitionistic metatheory, and results conditioned on unique choice or decidable equality where stated.
sections.unique_caveat: The decidability and acceptance-equivalence statements have explicit logical and finiteness hypotheses; the work does not provide an unrestricted equivalence test for all automata.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 0.75 from three cross-lists, including category theory and logic; the paper gives separation examples and equivalence criteria. No social-attention or citation component was recorded.

sections.title: Prophet Inequalities for Mixtures of I.I.D. Random Variables
sections.abstract: In a sequential selection problem with an unknown latent component governing conditionally i.i.d. nonnegative observations, the authors determine the best worst-case prophet-inequality factor as 1/e + 1/k^(2/3+o(1)).
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove that the largest universally guaranteed fraction of the expected maximum is 1/e + 1/k^(2/3+o(1)), with a secretary-rule lower bound and a common-scale-model upper-bound construction.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A latent index is drawn from a known prior over k component distributions; conditional on it, observations are i.i.d. from a known nonnegative distribution, while the index itself is not observed, and the expected maximum is finite.
sections.unique_caveat: The correction is asymptotic in the number of mixture components; the abstract does not give a simple exact finite-k guarantee.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 0.50 from two cross-lists, spanning algorithms and optimization alongside statistics; the matching upper and lower guarantee distinguishes it in this tier. No social-attention or citation component was recorded.

sections.title: The Kalton--Peck space disproves Rubio de Francia's conjecture
sections.abstract: The authors show that the complex Kalton--Peck space Z_2 is UMD but cannot be realized as a complex interpolation space between any UMD Banach space and a Hilbert space, giving a counterexample to Rubio de Francia's conjecture.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove that Z_2 is not isomorphic to [X,H]_theta for any UMD Banach space X, Hilbert space H, and 0 < theta < 1, and give a quotient-of-a-closed-subspace realization for each fixed interpolation parameter below one.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The result concerns the classical complex Kalton--Peck space and complex interpolation between a UMD space and a Hilbert space.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a counterexample to the stated interpolation conjecture, not a classification of all intermediate UMD spaces.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Collector score 0.25 from one cross-list into analysis of PDEs, below the multi-cross-list tiers. Included for its direct counterexample to a named conjecture, not as a popularity signal; no social-attention or citation component was recorded.
